what_happened: Research for this task found that the described root cause (a raw jq join("; ") on object-shaped blockers[], erroring and silently falling through to a detail-free fallback string via 2>/dev/null) was already superseded in this repository: an unrelated sibling task's uncommitted edit to the same line was swept into commit 83898819a (task 304's own commit), landing a map/if-object rendering expression that avoids the jq type error. That sibling task's own summary (specs/304_out_of_repo_pathspec_aborts_whole_commit/summaries/01_out-of-repo-pathspec-containment-summary.md) names this explicitly as 'an unconnected partial_blockers_detail jq enhancement' from the declared overlap set 184/263/273/279/284/285. This saved the implementation phase from needing to re-derive and land the core jq fix from scratch; remaining work is narrower: add the missing verbatim_goal field to the render, remove the now-defensive-only 2>/dev/null, extend test fixture 830 to assert on issues.jsonl content, and settle the class/severity/volume classification questions.

Carried-figure re-validation at plan time confirmed the research report's finding that the task description's stated root cause is no longer the live code: the partial) arm's partial_blockers_detail substitution already carries a map(if type == "object" ...) render, so the described raw join("; ") type error (reproduced here at exit 5 against a synthetic object-shaped blockers[] payload, and confirmed absent from the current expression, which exits 0) is not reachable from the expression as it stands. The description was written against a pre-fix state and overstates the defect; the residual, measurable defect is narrower -- verbatim_goal is never referenced by the render, so the single highest-value blocker subfield is still dropped. Planning proceeded against the narrower live defect rather than the described one, and the plan records the re-derivation explicitly so the implementer does not re-chase the superseded mechanism.

While adding the Phase 3 dedup regression fixture, candidate #832 was initially reused, colliding with an existing pre-migration fixture in the same test file that also uses candidate #832 (a user_decision regression). All tests still passed (setup_sandbox wipes WORKDIR per fixture, so there was no runtime collision), but the duplicate candidate number would have confused future maintainers grepping for a fixture by number. Caught before committing and renumbered to the unused candidate #833.
